promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Chemical bonds: ionic, covalent and metallic
How bonding and structure are related to properties
Structure and bonding of carbon: diamond, graphite and fullerenes

questions.q: Which type of bonding occurs between a metal and a non-metal?
questions.explain: Ionic bonding occurs when metals transfer electrons to non-metals, forming oppositely charged ions.

questions.q: Covalent bonding involves atoms that are:
questions.explain: Covalent bonds form between non-metal atoms that share pairs of electrons.

questions.q: When sodium forms an ionic bond with chlorine, what happens to the electrons?
options: Electrons are shared between the atoms
Sodium gains an electron from chlorine
Sodium transfers an electron to chlorine
Electrons are delocalised across both atoms
questions.explain: Sodium loses one electron to become Na+ and chlorine gains it to become Cl-, achieving full outer shells.

questions.q: In metallic bonding, the metal atoms are held together by attraction between positive ions and:
questions.explain: Metallic bonding is the strong attraction between positive metal ions and delocalised outer-shell electrons.

questions.q: Magnesium (group 2) reacts with oxygen (group 6) to form magnesium oxide. What is its formula?
questions.explain: Mg forms Mg2+ and O forms O2-, so they combine in a 1:1 ratio to give MgO.

questions.q: A calcium ion is Ca2+ and a chloride ion is Cl-. What is the formula of calcium chloride?
questions.explain: Two Cl- ions are needed to balance the 2+ charge on one Ca2+ ion, giving CaCl2.

questions.q: How many covalent bonds are there in a molecule of oxygen, O2?
questions.explain: Oxygen atoms share two pairs of electrons, forming a double covalent bond.

questions.q: Why do ionic compounds have high melting points?
options: Weak forces between molecules must be overcome
Strong electrostatic forces between oppositely charged ions must be overcome
Covalent bonds within molecules must be broken
questions.explain: The giant ionic lattice is held by strong electrostatic attractions requiring a lot of energy to break.

questions.q: Why can ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or dissolved but not when solid?
options: The ions gain a charge only when heated
The ions are free to move when molten or in solution
Covalent bonds break to release electrons
questions.explain: Charged ions can move and carry current only when the lattice breaks down on melting or dissolving.

questions.q: Simple molecular substances such as water and methane typically have:
options: The ability to conduct electricity when solid
questions.explain: Only weak intermolecular forces between the molecules need to be overcome, so melting and boiling points are low.

questions.q: When a simple molecular substance melts or boils, what is overcome?
options: The covalent bonds within the molecules
questions.explain: The strong covalent bonds inside molecules stay intact; only the weak forces between molecules are broken.

questions.q: Why are metals good conductors of electricity?
options: Their ions are free to move
They contain delocalised electrons that are free to move
questions.explain: Delocalised electrons move through the metal structure and carry electrical charge.

questions.q: Why are metals malleable (can be bent and shaped)?
options: Layers of metal ions can slide over each other
The ions repel each other strongly
questions.explain: The regular layers of positive ions can slide while remaining held together by delocalised electrons.

questions.q: In which state of matter do particles have the most energy and are furthest apart?
options: They are equal in all states
questions.explain: Gas particles have the most kinetic energy and are widely spaced with no regular arrangement.

questions.q: A substance conducts electricity when solid, has a very high melting point and is malleable. What is it most likely to be?
questions.explain: Conducting when solid, a high melting point and malleability are characteristic properties of metals.

questions.q: In diamond, each carbon atom is covalently bonded to how many other carbon atoms?
questions.explain: Each carbon in diamond forms four covalent bonds, giving a rigid giant covalent structure.

questions.q: Why is diamond very hard?
options: It has a giant covalent structure with many strong bonds
It is made of positive ions
questions.explain: The rigid network of strong covalent bonds makes diamond extremely hard.

questions.q: Why can graphite conduct electricity?
options: Each carbon atom bonds to four others
It has one delocalised electron per carbon atom that is free to move
Its ions are free to move
questions.explain: In graphite each carbon bonds to three others, leaving one delocalised electron per atom to carry charge.

questions.q: Why is graphite soft and slippery, making it useful as a lubricant?
options: It has a very high melting point
Its layers have no bonds between them and can slide over each other
It has a simple molecular structure
questions.explain: The layers are held only by weak forces, so they slide easily over one another.

questions.q: Which of the following is a fullerene made of carbon atoms arranged in cylinders?
questions.explain: Carbon nanotubes are cylindrical fullerenes with high tensile strength and useful electrical properties.
